column3: §FILM_FACT sheets / pile_w / pile_h / plan_gap · stage 0 of the raw set
column4: M: {sheets} drawings, exactly as drawn. No building yet.
column5: M: A common BricsCAD set: {sheets} drawings, exactly as drawn. | F: Where is the building? | M: There is none yet. Each sheet is its own flat world, one drawing unit is one millimetre. The pile spreads {pile_w} by {pile_h} metres, and the floor plan and the foundation plan sit {plan_gap} metres apart.

column3: §FILM_FACT sheets / steps / phase1 / phase2 / phase3 · start of the play on open
column4: M: Three passes over all {sheets} sheets: scale, orient, assemble.
column5: M: Now the system fills in what the drawings leave unsaid, in three passes over all {sheets} sheets. | F: How many steps? | M: {steps}. First every sheet is scaled to metres: {phase1} steps. Then each is oriented: {phase2}. Then they are assembled one after another onto the plan grid: {phase3}. The card at the bottom names the sheet and what was done to it.

column3: §FILM_FACT level_steps / level_value · the LEVEL steps of the play
column4: M: No plan states a level. Level {level_value}, in orange.
column5: M: {level_steps} plans state no level, and no title names a storey. | F: So what level do they get? | M: Level {level_value}, the ground, shown in orange. Orange is an inference, not a reading: you can type over it.

column3: §FILM_FACT play_s / tinted / tinted_inferred · after the play
column4: M: {tinted} sheets are tinted: placed by values not yet yours.
column5: M: {steps} steps in {play_s} seconds. {tinted} sheets are tinted, placed by values that are not yours yet, and {tinted_inferred} of them carry an orange inference. | F: Is anything written to the files? | M: Nothing. It is a view of what the drawings would become.

column3: §FILM_FACT open_yellow_rows / open_blocking / after_accept_blocking · Accept all, then Convert
column4: M: Accept all makes the yellow yours. Convert still refuses.
column5: M: Accept all makes the yellow yours: {open_yellow_rows} rows, and none left. | F: Can it convert now? | M: No. {open_blocking} items blocked it before, and {after_accept_blocking} still do. The list names each one. What the drawing does not say, it does not invent. What only a person knows, a person states.

column3: §FILM_FACT set_name / set_rows / after_set_blocking · the set name typed once
column4: M: First the set name: one word, {set_name}.
column5: M: First the set name: one word, {set_name}. | F: On every sheet? | M: Once. It becomes a yellow row on every sheet, {set_rows} rows, and Accept all takes them. {after_set_blocking} items are left.

column3: §FILM_FACT second_z / heights_typed · the height question and the second heights typed
column4: M: The panel asks for a second height, outlined in red.
column5: M: A height is the one thing a drawing cannot default. The panel asks for it, and outlines the empty fields in red. | F: What does it ask? | M: One height is known: the ground. Give a second: read a level text or a dimension on the sheet, type it in metres, and the y where it is drawn. Here {second_z} metres, on {heights_typed} sheets.

column3: §FILM_FACT layers_stated / after_layers_blocking · each layer's meaning chosen in the Layers section
column4: M: What each CAD layer is: {layers_stated} choices.
column5: M: Now what each CAD layer is. A drawing names layers, not meanings: Col, Fo, Dim, Wall. | F: How does it know a column from a footing? | M: It does not guess. You say it: {layers_stated} choices, sheet by sheet where a name means different things. Dim is a beam on the beam plan, and a net on the elevations. Then the blocking items fall to {after_layers_blocking}.

column3: §FILM_FACT bodyz_typed / bodies_before_exclude / bodies_after_exclude · body heights and the excluded area
column4: M: Two height ranges, and one stray area excluded.
column5: M: Two kinds of body no elevation shows need a height range, in metres: {bodyz_typed} typed. | F: And the stray area? | M: One box dragged on the beam plan excludes it. {bodies_before_exclude} bodies would be built before the box, {bodies_after_exclude} after.

column3: §FILM_FACT converted.n / n_columns / n_beams / n_footings / n_walls / n_slabs / n_roofs · Convert with the floor slab and roof ticked
column4: M: Convert, with the floor slab and the roof ticked: {converted.n} bodies.
column5: M: Convert, with the floor slab and the roof ticked: they are amber, estimated from the drawing's own evidence plus stated conventions. {converted.n} bodies: {n_columns} columns, {n_beams} beams, {n_footings} footings, {n_walls} walls, {n_slabs} floor slab, {n_roofs} roof pieces, and the members between. One shed from nine flat drawings: each value read from the drawing, defaulted and accepted, or stated by a person. | F: And then? | M: Then it is saved as an IFC, put in a database, and opened in the Viewer.
